newsitem.title: UK: Britain criticises Israel over new settlements.
newsitem.headline: Britain criticises Israel over new settlements.

text.p: Britain on Tuesday criticised Israel for starting to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in the face of fierce objections from the Palestinian community.
"The start of construction at Har Homa outside Jerusalem can do nothing but harm the peace process," Foreign Secretary (minister) Malcolm Rifkind said in a statement.

"Like all settlements, this one will be illegal, and it goes against the spirit of the Oslo Agreement. I am disappointed that the Israeli government have taken this decision against the strong advice of their friends in the international community."

Under the 1993 Oslo accord between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO), the future of Jerusalem and the fate of Jewish settlements was to be decided in talks that were supposed to have resumed on Monday.
Israeli bulldozers began work at Har Homa early on Tuesday, surrounded by soldiers to keep Palestinian protesters at bay.
The settlement will put another link into a chain of apartment blocks Israel has built to cement its hold on East Jerusalem and separate it from the rest of the West Bank.
Rifkind also urged Palestinians not to resort to violence over the building of the settlement.
"I urge the Palestinian leadership to continue to do everything possible to avoid current tensions leading to violence," he said.
"We are now at a crossroads in the peace process. If we are to continue on the road to peace, progress must be restored through the urgent resumption of dialogue and negotiation."
Earlier this month Britain expressed concern after Israel demanded that four Palestinian offices be closed down before it could carry out a scheduled withdrawal from the West Bank.
